pages.title: CAMP ECHO-4
pages.text: $(bold)ORSA FIELD REPORT$()$(br)Filed by: Sgt. Maren Holt$(br)Camp Designation: ECHO-4$(br2)Day 6. Radio contact with Tower Bravo lost at 0400. Interference consistent with atmospheric degradation. Switching to automated beacon protocol.$(br2)Supply levels nominal. Morale holding.

pages.title: Day 9
pages.text: Snow accumulation exceeding projections by 340%. Tent B collapsed overnight. Relocated Cpl. Vasquez to the command tent.$(br2)Radio still broadcasting on loop. No acknowledgment from any tower. Beginning to suspect we are the only camp still operational.$(br2)Food stores adequate for 12 more days at current rationing.

pages.title: Day 12
pages.text: Temperature dropped 18 degrees in six hours. Equipment freezing in place. The radio is the only thing still drawing power.$(br2)Vasquez says he heard voices on the frequency last night. I checked the logs. Nothing but static.$(br2)$(italic)I told him it was interference. I don't know if I believe that.$()

pages.title: Final Entry
pages.text: Day 14. Orders received: fall back to nearest tower for extraction.$(br2)Problem: nearest tower is 2km through whiteout conditions. Compass is unreliable. Wind chill below survivable threshold without EVA gear we don't have.$(br2)Leaving the radio on automated loop. If you're reading this, the radio still works. Follow the signal.$(br2)$(italic)- Holt$()
